previous_reply_acts.text: (is codex-17's answer adequate) Only partly. Its diagnosis is correct and matches what I found independently. (what it gets right)
- **Mechanism.** It's the same one I found by bisecting. `57848fe` replaced `head == "null"` with `is_structural_placeholder`, which leaves out the raw-syntax `null` that an omitted binder type produces.
- **Missed rule.** It names the 3-file rule the 17-file change broke.
- **Counterfactual.** Its check against the real `{α}` binder of `ReaderT.pure` is concrete, and it ran it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (first gap: the byte check) Our standing rule already required byte checks on constants that compile. A `ParserFn.run` probe from an empty cache at the merge `f8a3826` fails. I ran exactly that this afternoon, and it took 802 s. Its answer gets near this only as "relied too heavily on the preserved ParserFn artifact hash". In other words, an older generated file stood in for regenerating it. The fix is simple: the sentinel runs on the merge commit, from an empty cache, before the merge is accepted. Instead it proposes heavier review procedure: a census of consumers and a test per representation.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (second gap: after the fact) Its probe rows at `2ad2d88`, `2f6c1b6` and `79cd126` all show `ParserFn.run` failing after it had compiled. Each was logged as a "next independent stop", and each got a fix for that stop. One of those fixes, `79cd126`, compensated for `57848fe`. Bisecting `84dfff6` → `f8a3826` takes two probes, about 20 minutes run in parallel. That should have been the response the first time a compiling constant failed. The answer doesn't address this. That habit, treating a regression as progress, is what turned one bad merge into a morning of fixing symptoms.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (its proposed test) Its acceptance test asserts behaviour that is only true because of `79cd126`, the compensating fix. Adopting it would lock in the workaround, when the question should be whether `57848fe` belongs in integration at all.
